subject: maths
title: Primes, Factors & Multiples
welcome_lead: Numbers have hidden building blocks. Learn to spot primes, find factors, and list multiples like a pro.
meta_desc: Explore prime numbers, factors and multiples in this KS3 maths adventure.
final_note: Excellent! You can now break numbers down into their building blocks.

concepts.def: A whole number with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A number that divides exactly into another number.
The result of multiplying a number by an integer.
A whole number with more than two factors.
A factor that is also a prime number.
Two numbers that multiply to give a target number.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The first primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. Note that 2 is the only even prime.

To check if 21 is prime, try dividing by 2, 3, 5, 7. 21 = 3 × 7, so 21 is not prime.

To find factors of 12, find all pairs that multiply to 12: 1×12, 2×6, 3×4.

So the factors of 12 are: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

Multiples of 6 are: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36.

You get them by multiplying 6 by 1, 2, 3, 4, etc.
